code_snippet.title: FFmpeg Worker Optimization
code_snippet.code:
def process_video(file_path):
    # Optimized for low memory usage
    cmd = [
        'ffmpeg', '-i', file_path,
        '-c:v', 'libx264', '-preset', 'fast',
        '-crf', '22', '-c:a', 'aac',
        output_path
    ]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
code_snippet.explanation: We utilized a custom FFmpeg command with CRF (Constant Rate Factor) to balance quality and file size, reducing storage costs by 40%.

breakthrough.title: The 'Queue' Epiphany
breakthrough.description: Initially, we processed videos synchronously, which timed out requests. Switching to a RabbitMQ job queue decoupled the upload from processing, allowing the system to handle 1000+ concurrent uploads.

code_snippet.title: Adaptive Learning Graph
code_snippet.code:
MATCH (u:User {id: $userId})-[:COMPLETED]->(l:Lesson)
MATCH (l)-[:UNLOCKS]->(next:Lesson)
WHERE NOT (u)-[:COMPLETED]->(next)
RETURN next ORDER BY next.difficulty ASC LIMIT 1
code_snippet.explanation: We used Neo4j graph database to create dynamic learning paths. This query finds the next optimal lesson for a student based on what they've already mastered, rather than a linear list.

breakthrough.title: The 'Active' Classroom
breakthrough.description: We realized video calls weren't enough. We integrated a real-time collaborative code editor (Monaco) directly into the video stream, allowing instructors to 'pair program' with students instantly.

tech_reasoning.Neo4j: Chosen to model the complex dependencies between concepts in the adaptive curriculum.
tech_reasoning.WebRTC: Essential for low-latency video and data streaming in the live classroom.
tech_reasoning.GraphQL: Used to prevent over-fetching data when loading complex course structures.

projects.title: EchoMesh - Offline Disaster Communication
projects.solution: A decentralized, offline-first mobile app that allows communication without internet or cellular service. It creates a mesh network using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi Direct to hop messages between devices during disasters.

client_story.headline: Communication When the Grid Fails
client_story.subheadline: Connecting survivors when cell towers are down.
client_story.problem_statement: During natural disasters (Earthquakes, Floods) or network censorship, centralized communication fails. People get separated from loved ones with no way to contact them or share GPS coordinates.
client_story.solution_overview: EchoMesh transforms every phone into a 'node'. It uses the phone's Bluetooth and Wi-Fi radios to pass encrypted messages to nearby phones. These messages 'hop' from device to device until they reach the destination, creating a city-wide resilient network.

key_benefits.title: Multi-Hop Routing
key_benefits.description: Send a message to someone 1km away by hopping through 10 people.

key_benefits.title: SOS Broadcast
key_benefits.description: One-tap emergency beacon with your Medical ID.

case_study.overview: EchoMesh is a decentralized, offline-first mobile app that allows communication without internet or cellular service. It creates a mesh network using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi Direct to 'hop' encrypted messages between devices during disasters like hurricanes or earthquakes.

challenge.title: The Engineering Challenge
challenge.description: Smartphones are designed to connect to towers, not each other. Building a reliable mesh network on consumer Android/iOS phones is fighting against the OS's desire to sleep the radio to save battery. We needed a protocol that could route messages through 10+ devices without a central map.
pain_points: Battery Drain: Constant BLE scanning drains battery in < 3 hours
Cross-Platform Bridge: Connecting iOS (Multipeer) to Android (Wi-Fi Direct)
Routing Logic: Delivering a message to a moving target in a dynamic mesh
Security: Preventing bad actors from spoofing emergency beacons

solution.title: The Solution
solution.description: We implemented a custom 'Flooding with Deduplication' protocol (inspired by AODV) on top of the Bluetooth GATT layer. We also designed an intelligent duty-cycling system that sleeps the radio 90% of the time but wakes up in sync with neighbors.
key_features: Zero Infrastructure: Works in the middle of a desert or a blackout
Multi-Hop Routing: Messages hop from phone to phone to reach distant targets
SOS Broadcast: One-tap emergency beacon propagated with high priority
Geotagged Digital Drops: Leave virtual messages at a GPS location for rescuers

results.title: The Impact
results.description: Deployed during the 2024 floods, helping 500+ families locate each other.

code_snippet.title: BLE Packet Handler
code_snippet.explanation: This logic is the heart of the mesh. It checks 'Is this for me?'. If not, and the packet is still 'alive' (TTL > 0) and we haven't seen it before (deduplication), it acts as a good citizen and relays it to the next neighbor.

breakthrough.title: The 'Digital Breadcrumbs'
breakthrough.description: We added a feature where users can leave 'Geotagged Messages' virtually at a location. If another user walks past that spot later, their phone picks up the encrypted message from the ether (other nodes holding it). It's like leaving a persistent digital note on a wall for rescuers.

tech_reasoning.React Native: Allowed us to build the UI once, but we wrote extensive Native Modules (Java/Swift) to access the low-level radio hardware.
tech_reasoning.Realm: Chosen for its speed and offline-first synchronization capabilities.
tech_reasoning.Signal Protocol: Used for end-to-end encryption so even relay nodes cannot read private messages.

process.title: Field Testing
process.description: Tested in a dense forest with 20 volunteers to tune the signal range.

process.title: Protocol Optimization
process.description: Minimized packet headers to 5 bytes to maximize throughput on slow BLE.

process.title: UX Design
process.description: Designed high-contrast 'Dark Mode' to save battery on OLED screens.

testimonial.text: When the towers went down, EchoMesh was the only thing that worked. I found my brother because someone relayed his GPS signal to me. It literally saved lives.
testimonial.author: Maria Gonzales

case_study.final_notes: EchoMesh proves that technology can be resilient and humane, even when the world is chaos.
